subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Sound Adventure

points.label: Vowel A
points.text: Five special letters called vowels: A E I O U

slides.inSimpleWords: A is a special vowel sound we can sing!

image.alt: A is for Vowel — Vowels and Consonants

slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya sit in a circle and sing all five vowel sounds together!

slides.storyContext: Maya lists consonants: C, D, F, G, H... Arun makes all their sounds with her!

points.text: C D F G H J K L M N P R S T V W X Y Z

slides.inSimpleWords: Consonants are all the other letter sounds!

image.alt: More Consonants — Vowels and Consonants

example.solution: B + A = 'BA' — now it's a clear sound!

image.alt: Consonant + Vowel = Word — Vowels and Consonants

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya Make Sentences
hook: Watch Arun and Maya build their first sentences together!

slides.title: What is a Sentence?
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I like milk.' Maya says 'I like honey.' These are sentences!

points.label: Sentence
points.text: A sentence tells us a complete idea

slides.inSimpleWords: A sentence is words that tell us something!

image.alt: What is a Sentence? — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Sentences Need Words in Order
slides.storyContext: Maya says 'The cat sat.' Arun tries to say 'Sat the cat.' It sounds funny!

points.label: Word Order
points.text: Words in a sentence must be in the right order

slides.inSimpleWords: Words must go in the right order to make sense!

image.alt: Sentences Need Words in Order — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Who and What - Subject and Action
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'The boy runs.' 'The boy' is WHO, 'runs' is the ACTION.

points.label: Subject
points.text: 'The boy' tells us WHO

points.label: Action
points.text: 'runs' tells us WHAT they do

slides.inSimpleWords: Every sentence needs a WHO and a WHAT happens!

image.alt: Who and What - Subject and Action — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Simple Sentence Pattern
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches: Subject + Verb = Simple Sentence. She writes on the sand.

points.label: Pattern
points.text: WHO (subject) + DOES WHAT (verb) = sentence

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject and verb together make a complete sentence!

image.alt: Simple Sentence Pattern — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Making Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya practice together. Arun says a subject, Maya adds the action.

example.problem: I have words: 'dog', 'runs', 'the' — can we make a sentence?

slides.inSimpleWords: Subject + Verb = A sentence that makes sense!

image.alt: Making Sentences — Simple Sentences

slides.title: More Simple Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'The girl eats rice.' Maya says 'The bird flies high.' Both are perfect sentences!

points.label: Sentence 1
points.text: The girl eats rice.

points.label: Sentence 2
points.text: The bird flies high.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice making more sentences with your own ideas!

image.alt: More Simple Sentences — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Sentences Must End with a Period
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I see a butterfly' but forgets the period. Maya adds a dot at the end!

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: Every sentence ends with a period (.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always put a period at the end of a sentence!

image.alt: Sentences Must End with a Period — Simple Sentences

slides.title: Sentences Are Complete Thoughts
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write three sentences about their day on the wall!

points.label: Sentence 1
points.text: The sun shines brightly.

points.label: Sentence 2
points.text: We play in the garden.

points.label: Sentence 3
points.text: The wind blows gently.

slides.inSimpleWords: A sentence = WHO + DOES WHAT + period (.)!

image.alt: Sentences Are Complete Thoughts — Simple Sentences

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Big and Small Letter Quest
hook: Arun and Maya discover when to use big (capital) and small letters!

slides.title: Big Letters are Called CAPITALS
slides.storyContext: At school, the teacher shows Arun and Maya a big 'A' and a small 'a' on the board.

points.label: Capital Letter
points.text: The BIG letter form is called a CAPITAL letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Big letters are called CAPITAL letters!

image.alt: Big Letters are Called CAPITALS — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Every Sentence Starts with Capital
slides.storyContext: Maya reads: 'My name is Maya.' Arun points to the big 'M' at the start!

points.label: Rule 1
points.text: Every sentence ALWAYS starts with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Start sentences with a BIG capital letter!

image.alt: Every Sentence Starts with Capital — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Names Get Capital Letters
slides.storyContext: Arun writes his name: ARUN. Maya writes hers: MAYA. They use capitals!

points.label: Rule 2
points.text: Names of people ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Names start with capital letters always!

image.alt: Names Get Capital Letters — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Places Need Capitals Too
slides.storyContext: Maya says 'I live in Delhi.' Arun says 'I live in Mumbai.' Both cities start with capitals!

points.label: Rule 3
points.text: Names of places ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: City and country names start with capitals!

image.alt: Places Need Capitals Too — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Days and Months Need Capitals
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'Monday is the first day.' Maya says 'January is the first month.' Both use capitals!

points.label: Rule 4
points.text: Days and months ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Days and months start with big capital letters!

image.alt: Days and Months Need Capitals — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Capital or Small Letter?
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya play a game: when do we use capitals?

example.problem: Write: i like eating apples on monday
example.solution: I like eating apples on Monday. (Start + name 'I' + day 'Monday' need capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Capital at start, names, places, days, months!

image.alt: Capital or Small Letter? — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Small Letters for Most Words
slides.storyContext: Maya explains: most words use small letters in the middle of a sentence!

points.label: Rule 5
points.text: Words in the middle of sentences use SMALL letters

slides.inSimpleWords: Use small letters for most words in a sentence!

image.alt: Small Letters for Most Words — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Capital and Small Letters
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their 'Capital Letter Rules' poster!

points.label: Use CAPITALS for
points.text: Start of sentence, names, places, days, months

points.label: Use SMALL for
points.text: Most other words in the middle

slides.inSimpleWords: Capitals at start, names, places. Smalls for others!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Punctuation Adventure
hook: Learn the magic dots and marks that help sentences tell their story!

slides.title: The Period Stops the Sentence
slides.storyContext: Arun writes 'I like rice' and puts a dot. The sentence stops here!

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: A period stops a sentence. It means the idea is complete

slides.inSimpleWords: A period (.) ends a sentence with a complete idea!

image.alt: The Period Stops the Sentence — Punctuation

slides.title: Question Marks Ask Questions
slides.storyContext: Maya asks 'Do you like tea?' and puts a curvy mark with a dot.

points.label: Question Mark (?)
points.text: A question mark ends a sentence that ASKS something

slides.inSimpleWords: Question mark (?) ends a sentence that asks!

image.alt: Question Marks Ask Questions — Punctuation

slides.title: Exclamation Marks Show Feeling
slides.storyContext: Arun shouts 'What a big snake!' and uses a mark that shows his surprise!

points.label: Exclamation Mark (!)
points.text: An exclamation mark shows excitement or surprise

slides.inSimpleWords: Exclamation mark (!) shows big feelings and excitement!

image.alt: Exclamation Marks Show Feeling — Punctuation

slides.title: Three Sentence Ending Marks
slides.storyContext: Maya draws all three marks and explains when to use each one.

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: Normal sentence

points.label: Question (?)
points.text: Asking sentence

points.label: Exclamation (!)
points.text: Excited sentence

slides.inSimpleWords: Period stops. Question asks. Exclamation shows feeling!

image.alt: Three Sentence Ending Marks — Punctuation

slides.title: Comma Separates Ideas
slides.storyContext: Arun writes 'I like apples, mangoes, and bananas.' The commas help us pause!

points.label: Comma (,)
points.text: A comma separates words or ideas in a list

slides.inSimpleWords: Commas (,) separate items in a list!

image.alt: Comma Separates Ideas — Punctuation

slides.title: Using Punctuation Correctly
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya practice putting the right marks in the right places.

example.problem: I like rice bread and milk
example.solution: I like rice, bread, and milk. (commas separate the list)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use correct punctuation to make sentences clear!

image.alt: Using Punctuation Correctly — Punctuation

slides.title: More Punctuation Marks
slides.storyContext: Maya shows apostrophes (for 'can't') and quotation marks (for what people say)!

points.label: Apostrophe (')
points.text: Apostrophe shows missing letters: can't, don't

points.label: Quotation Marks ('')
points.text: Quotation marks show exactly what someone said

slides.inSimpleWords: Apostrophes and quotes help write correct sentences!

image.alt: More Punctuation Marks — Punctuation

slides.title: Punctuation Marks Matter
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a 'Punctuation Helper' chart for their classroom!

points.label: Separators
points.text: , (comma)

points.label: Special marks
points.text: ' (apostrophe), '' (quotes)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every punctuation mark has an important job!

image.alt: Punctuation Marks Matter — Punctuation

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's One and Many Adventure
hook: Discover how English words change when there's one thing or many things!

slides.title: Singular = One Thing
slides.storyContext: Arun holds up one apple. He says 'apple' — that's singular!

points.label: Singular
points.text: Singular means ONE thing or person

slides.inSimpleWords: Singular is the word for ONE thing!

image.alt: Singular = One Thing — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Plural = Many Things
slides.storyContext: Maya holds up five apples. She says 'apples' — that's plural!

points.label: Plural
points.text: Plural means MORE than ONE (many things)

slides.inSimpleWords: Plural is the word for MANY things!

image.alt: Plural = Many Things — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Most Plurals Add 's'
slides.storyContext: Arun shows: one cat is 'cat', many cats are 'cats'. Just add 's'!

points.label: Add s
points.text: cat → cats, book → books, dog → dogs

slides.inSimpleWords: Add 's' to most words to make them plural!

image.alt: Most Plurals Add 's' — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Words Ending in 'x, z, s' Add 'es'
slides.storyContext: Maya shows: box → boxes, buzz → buzzes, class → classes!

points.label: Add es
points.text: Words ending in x, z, s, sh, ch add 'es'

slides.inSimpleWords: Add 'es' to words ending in x, z, s, sh, ch!

image.alt: Words Ending in 'x, z, s' Add 'es' — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Words Ending in 'y' Change
slides.storyContext: Arun says: one baby, many babies. The 'y' becomes 'ies'!

points.label: y to ies
points.text: baby → babies, lady → ladies, city → cities

slides.inSimpleWords: Change 'y' to 'ies' for words ending in consonant+y!

image.alt: Words Ending in 'y' Change — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Irregular Plurals
slides.storyContext: Maya shows words that don't follow the rules!

example.problem: Singular: child, foot, tooth, person. Plural?
example.solution: children, feet, teeth, people. These are IRREGULAR!

slides.inSimpleWords: Some words change completely to make plural!

image.alt: Irregular Plurals — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Practice with Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I have one book.' Maya says 'I have many books.'

points.label: Singular sentence
points.text: The boy plays.

points.label: Plural sentence
points.text: The boys play.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use singular and plural words in your sentences!

image.alt: Practice with Sentences — Singular and Plural

slides.title: Singular and Plural
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya make a list of singular and plural word pairs!

points.label: Add s
points.text: cat → cats, book → books

points.label: Add es
points.text: box → boxes, class → classes

points.label: Irregular
points.text: child → children, foot → feet

slides.inSimpleWords: One thing = singular. Many = plural. Learn the rules!

image.alt: Singular and Plural — Singular and Plural

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Noun and Pronoun Journey
hook: Learn how nouns name things and pronouns replace them!

slides.title: What is a Noun?
slides.storyContext: Arun points: 'Look! A dog, a tree, a house! These are all nouns — they name things!'

points.label: Noun
points.text: A word that names a person, place, animal, or thing

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns are words that name people, places, things!

image.alt: What is a Noun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name People
slides.storyContext: Maya lists: 'Arun, teacher, doctor, mother — these are nouns for people!'

points.label: Person nouns
points.text: boy, girl, teacher, doctor, mother, farmer, police

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name people are person words!

image.alt: Nouns Name People — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name Places
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Delhi, school, park, temple — these are places. All nouns!'

points.label: Place nouns
points.text: city, school, park, temple, library, garden, beach

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name places are place words!

image.alt: Nouns Name Places — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name Animals and Things
slides.storyContext: Maya points to things: 'Dog, cat, book, pencil, chair — all nouns!'

points.label: Animal and thing nouns
points.text: dog, cat, bird, book, pencil, chair, table, toy

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name animals and objects too!

image.alt: Nouns Name Animals and Things — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: What is a Pronoun?
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Instead of saying Arun every time, I say I or me. That's a pronoun!'

points.label: Pronoun
points.text: A word that replaces a noun

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns replace nouns in sentences!

image.alt: What is a Pronoun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: I, You, He, She, It, We, They
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches the main pronouns: 'I am Maya. You are my friend. He is Arun. She/It/We/They too!'

points.label: Personal pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they

slides.inSimpleWords: I, you, he, she, it, we, they are pronouns!

image.alt: I, You, He, She, It, We, They — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns
slides.storyContext: Arun shows how to replace nouns with pronouns!

example.problem: Maya likes books. Maya reads books. Maya writes about books.
example.solution: Maya likes books. She reads them. She writes about them. (She replaces Maya, them replaces books)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use pronouns to avoid repeating the noun!

image.alt: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'This is my pencil. That is your book. This is his toy. That's her doll.'

points.label: Possessive pronouns
points.text: my, your, his, her, its, our, their

slides.inSimpleWords: Possessive pronouns show who owns something!

image.alt: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns and Pronouns
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a chart showing nouns and their pronoun replacements!

points.label: Nouns
points.text: Name people, places, animals, things

points.label: Pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (replace nouns)

points.label: Possessives
points.text: my, your, his, her, our, their (show who owns)

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name. Pronouns replace. Both are important!

image.alt: Nouns and Pronouns — Nouns and Pronouns

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Action-Packed Verb Adventure
hook: Discover verbs — the words that show action and movement!

slides.title: What is a Verb?
slides.storyContext: Arun jumps and says 'Jump! That's a verb — an action word!' Maya runs and shouts 'Run!'

points.label: Verb
points.text: A word that shows action or what someone does

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are action words that show doing!

image.alt: What is a Verb? — Verbs

slides.title: Run, Jump, Eat, Sleep
slides.storyContext: Maya makes a list: 'I run, I jump, I eat, I sleep — all verbs that show what I do!'

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: run, jump, eat, sleep, play, walk, dance, sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Run, jump, eat are all action verbs!

image.alt: Run, Jump, Eat, Sleep — Verbs

slides.title: Write, Read, Draw, Think
slides.storyContext: Arun does homework: 'I write answers, I read questions, I draw pictures, I think carefully!'

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: write, read, draw, think, learn, understand, remember

slides.inSimpleWords: Write, read, draw, think show different actions!

image.alt: Write, Read, Draw, Think — Verbs

slides.title: Can, Help, Give, Take
slides.storyContext: Maya helps Arun: 'I can lift this! I help my friend! I give him a pencil. He takes it!'

points.label: More verbs
points.text: can, help, give, take, make, build, break, fix

slides.inSimpleWords: Help, give, take show actions between people!

image.alt: Can, Help, Give, Take — Verbs

slides.title: Being Verbs: Is, Are, Am, Was, Were
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'I am happy. She is smart. They are friends. I was sleepy. We were tired!'

points.label: Being verbs
points.text: is, are, am, was, were (show state of being, not action)

slides.inSimpleWords: Being verbs show who or what something is!

image.alt: Being Verbs: Is, Are, Am, Was, Were — Verbs

slides.title: Verbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write sentences using different verbs!

example.problem: Complete these: The cat ___. The boy ___. She ___ milk.
example.solution: The cat sleeps. The boy plays. She drinks milk. (sleeps, plays, drinks are verbs)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every sentence needs a verb to show action!

image.alt: Verbs in Sentences — Verbs

slides.title: Verbs Can Change
slides.storyContext: Maya shows: 'I play today. I played yesterday. I will play tomorrow. The verb changes with time!'

points.label: Verb tenses
points.text: play (now), played (past), will play (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs change when we talk about different times!

image.alt: Verbs Can Change — Verbs

slides.title: Verbs Show Action
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya make a poster of all their favorite action verbs!

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: run, jump, eat, write, read, play, dance, sing

points.label: Being verbs
points.text: is, are, am, was, were

points.label: Verb tenses
points.text: present, past, future (changes with time)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are the most important words in sentences!

image.alt: Verbs Show Action — Verbs

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Describing Word Adventure
hook: Learn adjectives — words that describe how things look, feel, and are!

slides.title: What is an Adjective?
slides.storyContext: Arun holds a big red apple. 'Big and red — these words describe the apple!' says Maya.

points.label: Adjective
points.text: A word that describes a noun (how it looks, feels, or is)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives are describing words for nouns!

image.alt: What is an Adjective? — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Size
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'This is a big house. This is a small house. Big and small describe size!'

points.label: Size adjectives
points.text: big, small, large, tiny, huge, long, short, wide, narrow

slides.inSimpleWords: Big, small, tiny describe how big something is!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Size — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Color
slides.storyContext: Maya paints: 'A red heart, a blue sky, a yellow sun, a green tree!'

points.label: Color adjectives
points.text: red, blue, yellow, green, orange, purple, pink, black, white

slides.inSimpleWords: Red, blue, green describe the color of things!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Color — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Feelings
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'I feel happy. The movie is funny. The noise is loud and scary!'

points.label: Feeling adjectives
points.text: happy, sad, funny, scary, brave, shy, angry, friendly

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives can describe feelings too!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Feelings — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Texture and Taste
slides.storyContext: Maya touches a smooth silk cloth and a rough rope. Arun tastes sweet candy and sour lemon!

points.label: Texture/taste
points.text: soft, hard, smooth, rough, wet, dry, sweet, sour, spicy, delicious

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives describe how things feel and taste!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Texture and Taste — Adjectives

slides.title: Using Adjectives in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write sentences with lots of describing words!

example.problem: Write: 'I have a dog.' Add adjectives to make it more interesting.
example.solution: I have a big, brown, friendly dog. (big, brown, friendly are adjectives)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make sentences more interesting!

image.alt: Using Adjectives in Sentences — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Numbers and More
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'I have one apple, three books, many toys, few pencils, first place, last runner!'

points.label: More adjectives
points.text: one, two, many, few, first, last, new, old, good, bad, beautiful, ugly

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives describe numbers and qualities too!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Numbers and More — Adjectives

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Everything
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write a colorful story full of describing words!

points.label: Size and shape
points.text: big, small, long, short, round, square

points.label: Color
points.text: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple

points.label: Feelings and qualities
points.text: happy, sad, beautiful, ugly, good, bad, brave, shy

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make describing easier and fun!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Everything — Adjectives

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Time Travel Tenses
hook: Journey through past, present, and future with verbs that change with time!

slides.title: What is Tense?
slides.storyContext: Arun explains: 'Tense shows WHEN an action happens — now, yesterday, or tomorrow!'

points.label: Tense
points.text: The time when an action happens (past, present, or future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Tense tells us WHEN something happens!

image.alt: What is Tense? — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Present Tense: Right Now
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'I play now. I eat now. I read now. This is PRESENT TENSE!'

points.label: Present tense
points.text: Action happening RIGHT NOW: play, eat, read, run, jump, sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Present tense = action happening RIGHT NOW!

image.alt: Present Tense: Right Now — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Past Tense: Yesterday
slides.storyContext: Arun remembers: 'I played yesterday. I ate yesterday. I read yesterday. This is PAST TENSE!'

points.label: Past tense
points.text: Action that already happened: played, ate, read, ran, jumped, sang

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense = action that already happened!

image.alt: Past Tense: Yesterday — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Future Tense: Tomorrow
slides.storyContext: Maya dreams: 'I will play tomorrow. I will eat tomorrow. I will read tomorrow. FUTURE TENSE!'

points.label: Future tense
points.text: Action that will happen: will play, will eat, will read, will run

slides.inSimpleWords: Future tense = action that will happen!

image.alt: Future Tense: Tomorrow — Tenses Basic

slides.title: How Verbs Change with Tense
slides.storyContext: Arun shows how the same action verb changes: play (now), played (before), will play (later)!

points.label: Present
points.text: play, eat, run, read

points.label: Past
points.text: played, ate, ran, read

points.label: Future
points.text: will play, will eat, will run, will read

slides.inSimpleWords: The same verb changes form for each time!

image.alt: How Verbs Change with Tense — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Using All Three Tenses
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write about the same action in past, present, and future!

example.problem: Write sentences with 'eat': past, now, and future.
example.solution: I ate rice yesterday. I eat rice today. I will eat rice tomorrow. (ate, eat, will eat)

slides.inSimpleWords: Same verb, different tense = different time!

image.alt: Using All Three Tenses — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Irregular Verbs: Special Ones
slides.storyContext: Maya shows verbs that don't follow the normal rules: go/went/will go, eat/ate/will eat, run/ran/will run!

points.label: Irregular verbs
points.text: go→went, eat→ate, run→ran, is→was, have→had (don't add 'ed')

slides.inSimpleWords: Some verbs change in special ways in past!

image.alt: Irregular Verbs: Special Ones — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Three Tenses, Three Times
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a timeline showing past, present, and future actions!

points.label: Past tense
points.text: Yesterday: I played, I ate, I ran, I read

points.label: Present tense
points.text: Now: I play, I eat, I run, I read

points.label: Future tense
points.text: Tomorrow: I will play, I will eat, I will run

slides.inSimpleWords: Past = done. Present = now. Future = coming soon!

image.alt: Three Tenses, Three Times — Tenses Basic
